listeningScripts.title: Airline Baggage Delay
listeningScripts.text: Passenger: Excuse me, my baggage didn't arrive on my flight from Vancouver. Airline Agent: I'm very sorry to hear that. Let me help you file a report. What is your confirmation number? Passenger: It's VH-4829. I arrived about an hour ago on flight AC-127. Agent: Got it. Did you check your bag through to your final destination or pick it up here in Calgary? Passenger: I checked it all the way to Calgary. I have the baggage claim ticket right here. Agent: Perfect. Can I see that? The tag number is LM-58493. Your bag is a black Samsonite roller, correct? Passenger: Yes, that's right. It has a red ribbon on the handle. Agent: Great. I've found it in the system. It actually came off the plane but was misrouted to Edmonton by mistake. It's on the next flight back to Calgary, which arrives at 6:15 PM tonight. Passenger: So I'll have it this evening? Agent: Yes, we'll have it delivered to your hotel by 8 PM. Where are you staying? Passenger: The Fairmont Palliser downtown. What compensation will I get? Agent: Because the delay is less than 24 hours and the bag will be delivered today, we'll provide a $50 travel voucher for your next flight with us.

listeningScripts.title: Apartment Viewing Discussion
listeningScripts.text: Renter: I'm interested in this one-bedroom apartment. What are the lease terms? Landlord: It's a one-year lease. The rent is $1,200 per month, due on the first of each month. Renter: That seems reasonable. What utilities are included? Landlord: Water and heating are included, but you pay for electricity and internet. Renter: I see. What about parking? Landlord: There's one dedicated parking spot in the lot. It's included in the rent. Renter: Perfect. When would I be able to move in? Landlord: If we sign the lease today, you can move in on July 1st. Renter: Is that two weeks from now? Landlord: Yes, exactly two weeks. Do you have any pets? Renter: I have a cat. Is that okay? Landlord: Yes, cats are allowed. There's a one-time pet deposit of $150. Renter: Alright. Can I get a few days to think about it? Landlord: Sure, take until the end of the week. After that, I have other interested renters.

listeningScripts.title: Travel Insurance Information Session
listeningScripts.text: Welcome to our travel insurance information session. Today, I'll explain the coverage options available through our travel agency. We offer three plans: Basic, Standard, and Premium. The Basic plan covers medical emergencies, emergency dental, and evacuation. Cost is seventy-five dollars for two weeks. The Standard plan includes everything in Basic plus trip cancellation coverage, lost luggage reimbursement up to one thousand dollars, and travel delays over twelve hours. Cost is one hundred twenty dollars for two weeks. The Premium plan is our comprehensive option. It adds accidental death coverage, zero deductible for medical claims, and upgrade to two thousand five hundred dollars for lost luggage. Premium costs two hundred twenty dollars for two weeks. All plans exclude claims related to alcohol impairment or pre-existing medical conditions not disclosed. Coverage begins on your departure date and ends upon return. Claims must be filed within ninety days of the incident. You'll receive a confirmation email with your policy documents. For claims, call our toll-free number at 1-800-555-0147. Representatives are available 24/7. Questions about coverage should be directed to our customer service team. Purchase your policy at least seven days before travel.

listeningScripts.title: Winnipeg Public Transit Modernization
listeningScripts.text: Winnipeg is modernizing its public transit system with a 450 million dollar investment over the next decade. The city has approved plans to purchase 300 new electric buses to replace aging diesel vehicles. The transition will eliminate approximately 8,500 tonnes of annual carbon emissions from the transportation sector. Current ridership stands at 89 million trips annually, and the city expects this to grow by 20 percent once new services launch. Construction of a new rapid transit corridor connecting downtown to the airport is set to begin next year. This corridor will reduce travel time from downtown to the airport from 45 minutes to just 22 minutes. The project includes the construction of 12 new transit stations along the corridor. Free transit passes will be offered to seniors and students to encourage ridership. Overall, the modernization is expected to create 1,100 permanent jobs in operations and maintenance. Winnipeg Transit has committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2040.

listeningScripts.title: Community Center Renovation Project
listeningScripts.text:
Recreation Director Karen: We're finally moving forward with the community center renovation that was approved last year. The project is budgeted at 6.8 million dollars and should take about 18 months to complete. We plan to add a new fitness center, upgrade the swimming pool, and create additional youth programming spaces. This will significantly improve our facilities.

Community Member Robert: I'm glad to see this moving forward, Karen, but I'm concerned about one thing. During the construction, the center will be partially closed. My kids attend after-school programs here, and I'm worried about where they'll go during the renovation period. Many families in our community rely on these programs for childcare.

Operations Manager Susan: That's a valid concern, Robert. We've actually planned for this. We'll maintain the community room and outdoor spaces throughout the project. We can relocate the after-school programs there during construction, though it will be more crowded. We're also negotiating with the school district to potentially use school facilities as a backup location for some activities.

Youth Program Coordinator Jason: I'm excited about the upgrades, especially the new youth spaces. But Susan, we need to be realistic about the outdoor space. We currently use it for sports and recreation. If we're moving programs there, we'll have limited room for physical activities. Could we consider using a local park for some outdoor programming during construction?

listeningScripts.title: Algorithmic Bias in Hiring Systems
listeningScripts.text: Algorithmic bias in hiring is a serious problem that companies are using as a shortcut without taking responsibility for the consequences. Many organizations now use AI systems to screen resumes, assess candidate fit, and predict job performance. These systems seem objective—they're just mathematics, right? Wrong. These algorithms are trained on historical data, which includes decades of human bias. If women were historically excluded from leadership positions, the algorithm learns that pattern and replicates it. If certain demographics were underrepresented in technical roles, the algorithm reinforces that exclusion. Studies have documented this repeatedly. Amazon famously scrapped their hiring algorithm when they discovered it was discriminating against women. Google's recruiting algorithm showed bias against applicants from historically black colleges. These weren't intentional—that's precisely the problem. The systems' creators didn't set out to discriminate; they just trusted that math was unbiased, when in reality, data is never neutral. My argument is this: companies should not deploy algorithmic hiring systems without rigorous bias testing and external auditing. If you use an algorithm to screen candidates, you're making a business decision, and you're responsible for its outcomes. You can't hide behind the algorithm or claim you didn't know it was biased. Moreover, algorithms eliminate human judgment, nuance, and chance. They can't capture potential, resilience, or growth. Some of the most successful employees wouldn't have passed an algorithm. We need a return to more human-centered hiring while using algorithms cautiously and with oversight.
